newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firmer on capital inflow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firmer on capital inflow.

text.p: The Mexican peso extended midday firmness at the close of trade on Thursday, after dealers continued to switch to pesos to enter the local stock and money markets, traders said.
"Locals bought some dollars to square their books this morning, but foreigners stepped in later to sell," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 1.1 and 1.7 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8715/7.8750 and 7.8620/7.8670 per dollar.
Dealers said capital flow, which began after relatively smooth mid-term elections held on Sunday, slowed in early trade but resumed after strong trade data were released at mid-session.

Foreign buyers pushed up the local bourse's blue chip IPC index by 32.88 points to 4,869.37. In the money market, overnight Cetes rates plummeted 630 basis points to 17.20 percent, partly due to demand.
The Finance Ministry revised May trade balance figures up to $220 million from a preliminary $88 million.
Dealers said the data helped ease fears the peso was not competitively priced and possibly about to suffer from a slide following the elections.
They added memories in the market were still fresh of how a burgeoning trade gap in 1994 helped bring about a shock devaluation and a financial collapse.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 1.7 centavos firmer at 7.8700/7.8740 per dollar.
Dealers meanwhile said the strong peso had led Banco de Mexico to hold an auction of dollar puts on Wednesday for $300 million in addition to their usual month-end auction.
Officials at Banco de Mexico were not immediately available for comment.
